Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat al-Hashr

It is Madaniyyah (revealed in Madinah).

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he named it Surat al-Nadir, and Allah knows best.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah﴾. That is: prays and worships Allah. Tasbih (glorification) of Allah, exalted is He, is declaring Him free of every imperfection. Some of them mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: every tasbih that occurs in the Qur'an means salah (prayer). From this is his saying: subhat al-duha, that is, the prayer of the forenoon (salat al-duha).

And His saying: ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾. That is: the Overpowering over things, the Wise in matters.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 2:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes﴾. The commentators (mufassirun) in general said: they are the Banu al-Nadir from the Jews. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had made a truce with them and stipulated that they would not support the idolaters of Quraysh, but they broke the covenant. It is narrated that their breaking of the covenant was that the Prophet (ﷺ) came to them seeking their help regarding the blood-money (diya) of the two men, the Taladiyin, and it is said the Amiriyin, who were killed by Amr ibn Umayya al-Damri. He came and sat at the base of their fortress. They said: "What brings you, O Muhammad?" He mentioned to them what had brought him and sought their help. They then plotted to drop a boulder upon him and kill him. Gabriel (peace be upon him) came and informed him, so he returned to Medina, then besieged them and expelled them.

And His saying: ﴿at the first gathering﴾. Al-Hasan said: the meaning of "the first gathering" is that al-Sham is the land of gathering and assembly, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) expelled them to al-Sham. So his expelling them was the first gathering, and the second gathering is on the Day of Resurrection. This is also the view of Ikrimah. Ikrimah said: whoever doubts that al-Sham is the land of the gathering, let him recite His saying: ﴿at the first gathering﴾. It is also said: the Banu al-Nadir were the first of the Jews to be expelled from their lands, so He said: ﴿at the first gathering﴾ in this sense. Then Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, expelled the remaining Jews from the Arabian Peninsula, relying on the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): "Two religions shall not coexist in the Arabian Peninsula." Abu Ubayda said: the Arabian Peninsula extends in length from the well of Abu Musa to the farthest stone in Yemen, and in breadth from the sands of Yabrin to the end of the Samawa. The second view is that of Mujahid and others.

And His saying: ﴿You did not think that they would go forth﴾. Its meaning: you did not think, O believers, that they would go forth, because they were the most powerful of the Jews in the land of the Hijaz and the most secure in their position.

His saying: ﴿And they thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allah﴾, that is: from the punishment of Allah.

And His saying: ﴿But Allah came at them from where they did not expect﴾. Al-Suddi said: it was by the killing of Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf. Muhammad ibn Maslama al-Ansari killed him when the Messenger of Allah sent him, and he had been a friend of Ka'b in the pre-Islamic era. He came to him at night and knocked on the door of the fortress, so Ka'b came down, and he ambushed and killed him. It is narrated that Muhammad ibn Maslama said to Ka'b: "Did you not used to promise us the emergence of this Prophet, and say: 'He is the one who laughs much, who fights, who rides the camel, who wears a shawl, who is content with a morsel, whose sword is on his shoulder, who has battles and battles'?" Ka'b said: "Yes, but he is not that one." Muhammad said: "You lie, O enemy of Allah; rather you envied him."

And His saying: ﴿And He cast terror into their hearts﴾, that is: fear. It is established that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I have been supported with terror over a distance of a month's journey."

And His saying: ﴿They destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers﴾. It was recited as "yukhribuna" from the causative (ikhrab). Some said the two are one, and the intensive form (tashdid) is for multiplication. Abu Amr said: "yukhribuna" is from the verb "takhrib" (causing ruin), and "yakhribuna" with light vowelling means they leave them in ruin. If it is asked: how did He say "they destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers," when it is not conceivable that they destroyed their houses by the hands of the believers? The answer: He attributed it to them only because they were the ones who compelled the believers to destruction and forced them to it through their refusal to believe. If someone says: why did they destroy their own houses? We say: they sought by that to widen the place of battle. It is related from al-Zuhri that the Muslims were destroying from outside the fortress, while the Jews were destroying from inside it, and their destruction was so that they could carry with them what they found admirable of the roof-beams of their houses. It is also said: so that nothing would remain for the believers.

And His saying: ﴿So take warning, O you with vision﴾. "I'tibar" is considering a thing so as to know its kind and its like. It is also said its meaning is: reflect and ponder, O people of intellect and understanding, how Allah gave the believers power over them and gave them power over themselves. This verse has been used as evidence for the permissibility of analogical reasoning (qiyas) in legal rulings, because qiyas is a form of i'tibar; for it is the conveying of one thing to its like through a common meaning joining them, so that the two agree in the ruling of the Sharia.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 3:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Had Allah not decreed exile for them, He would surely have punished them in this world﴾, meaning: by the sword. Some scholars have used this verse to argue that expulsion from the homeland is equivalent to killing; and the Exalted's words ﴿Kill yourselves or leave your homes﴾ point to this as well.

And His words: ﴿And for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire﴾, meaning: the punishment of Jahannam (Hell).

This is the commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 4:

Regarding His the Exalted's words: ﴿That is because they opposed (shaqqu) Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning: they opposed Allah and His Messenger. We have already mentioned that its meaning is: they became on a side (shiqq) other than the side of the believers.

And His words: ﴿And whoever opposes (yushaqqi) Allah﴾, meaning: opposes Allah, ﴿indeed, Allah is severe in punishment﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down (ma qata'tum min lina)﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: al-lina (the palm-tree, lina) is every date other than the barni and the 'ajwa, and the people of Madina call the dates al-alwan (the varieties). It was also said: al-lina is the palm tree (al-nakhla). It is reported from some of them that al-lina is a collective term for trees, and it was named lina because of its softness (linha) with life. It is reported from Sufyan that he said: al-lina refers to the noblest palms. It was also said: it is the young palm shoot (al-fasil), and it was named lina because it does not grow in intense heat. Among the well-known reports is that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The 'ajwa is from Paradise, and in it is a cure from poison."

In the account (al-qissa): when the Companions of the Messenger of God besieged Banu al-Nadir, some of them cut down the palm trees and some of them left them standing.

In a report: "The Prophet commanded them to cut down the palm trees, so the Jews went out when they saw that and said: 'O Muhammad, did you not forbid corruption, and is this not corruption?' So God, may He be exalted, revealed this verse."

It has been established by the transmission of Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that "the Prophet burned and cut down the palm trees of Banu al-Nadir, so God, may He be exalted, revealed: ﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down, or left standing on their roots, it was by the permission of God﴾," i.e., by the command of God. He (may God be pleased with him) said: al-Makki ibn 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us of this report, from my grandfather, from al-Farabri, from al-Bukhari, from Qutayba, from al-Layth ibn Sa'd, from Nafi', the report... 

In another report: the Prophet burned al-Buwayra, and their poet said a poem:

(And the burning of al-Buwayra, spreading far, became cheap in the eyes of the nobles of Banu Lu'ayy...)

Al-Buwayra is the place of Banu al-Nadir. His saying: ﴿and that He may disgrace the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqin)﴾ refers to the Jews, and their disgrace is their seeing how the believers have power over their wealth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 6:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them﴾, i.e., from the Banu al-Nadir. The fay' (fay', booty gained without battle) is every property that Allah, exalted is He, returned from the disbelievers to the Muslims. It is derived from the meaning of "return": one says "fa'a" when he returns, and from it comes "fay' al-zill" (the shade that returns after the sun has passed its zenith). The difference between fay' and ghanima (ghanima, spoils won by battle) is that ghanima is what the Muslims take from the disbelievers by means of the pressing of horses and mounts, whereas fay' is what reaches the Muslims of the disbelievers' property without the pressing of horses and mounts.

And His saying: ﴿You did not press upon it with horse or riding camel﴾. The rikab (rikab, riding camels) are the camels, and the meaning is: their property came to the Messenger of Allah without your pressing upon it with horses or camels. Al-iyjaf (iyjaf, pressing forward at speed) is hastening. Allah, exalted is He, therefore made the property of the Banu al-Nadir exclusively for the Prophet, because the Prophet prevailed over them without fighting by the Muslims, and he would set aside from it the provision of a year for his household, and what remained he would use for horses (al-kura') and equipment in the way of Allah.

In the tafsir of Qatada: the Muslims asked that it be divided among them, so Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse and made what they had obtained exclusively for the Messenger. When the Messenger of Allah expelled them, he stipulated that they could take what their camels could carry, except the hilqa (hilqa, weapons), that is, the arms.

And His saying: ﴿But Allah gives His messengers power over whomever He wills﴾, i.e., He gives power to His Messenger over whomever He wills.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾, i.e., capable.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 7:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whatever Allah has restored to His Messenger from the people of the townships, it belongs to Allah and to the Messenger, and to the near of kin, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer﴾. In the verse is an explanation of the destinations of the khums (one-fifth), and We have explained it before. The "townships" (al-qura) are the Arabian towns, such as Khaybar, Wadi al-Qura, Fayma', and others. Also well known in tafsir is that the Prophet distributed the wealth of the Banu al-Nadir among the Muhajirun, and gave none of it to the Ansar except three men: Sahl ibn Hunayf, Abu Dujana, and al-Harith ibn al-Simma. This is a view other than the first one we mentioned, and it is the more well known. Accordingly, Allah made the wealth of the Banu al-Nadir exclusively for the Messenger, to distribute among the Muhajirun so that they would suffice the Ansar's needs.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So that it does not become a circulating commodity among the rich among you﴾, meaning: lest the rich among you pass it around among themselves. Tadawul (circulation) is the transfer from one hand to another.

His saying: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾. In this verse Allah, exalted is He, urges the Muslims to submit to the command and prohibition of Allah, exalted is He, because the meaning is: whatever the Messenger brings you from Allah, take it, and whatever he forbids you from Allah, refrain from it.

His saying: ﴿And fear Allah; indeed Allah is severe in punishment﴾, meaning: in retribution.

For the Quranic verse: "[It is] for the poor emigrants (lil-fuqara' al-muhajirin)", meaning: what Allah gave as spoils (afa'a) to His Messenger is for the poor emigrants, "who were expelled from their homes and their wealth."

"Their homes" (diyarihim) refers to Makkah and others, and "their wealth" refers to what they left behind at the time of their emigration (hijra).

His saying: "Seeking bounty from Allah and His pleasure" means: they seek the bounty of Allah and His good pleasure.

His saying: "And they support Allah and His Messenger. Those are the truthful" means: the truthful in conviction (aqd), in speech (qawl), and in action (fi'l).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 9:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And those who had settled in the abode [of Hijrah] and in faith before them﴾. The exegetes unanimously agreed that the intended people are the Ansar (the Helpers).

﴿And in faith before them love those who emigrate to them, and do not find in their breasts any need for what they have been given, and prefer them over themselves, even though they themselves were in privation. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul – it is those who are the successful.﴾

His saying: ﴿had settled in the abode and in faith﴾ means: they made their home in Madinah and embraced faith. It was also said: ﴿had settled in the abode﴾ means: they prepared the homes for the emigrants and consoled them with all their wealth.

His saying: ﴿and in faith﴾ means: they made their homes abodes of faith, by their manifesting faith among themselves. If it is asked: how is His saying ﴿before them﴾ consistent, when the Ansar only believed after the Muhajirun? The answer: His saying ﴿before them﴾ refers to settling in the abode, not to faith. Secondly, even if it refers to faith, what is meant is before their emigration, since the Ansar had believed before their emigration.

His saying: ﴿love those who emigrate to them﴾ means: from the people of Makkah and others.

His saying: ﴿and do not find in their breasts any need for what they have been given﴾. Qatadah said, and many of the exegetes said, its meaning is: envy of what they were given. It was also said: constriction in their hearts regarding what was given to the Muhajirun, and this has the same meaning as the first. We have already mentioned what the Messenger of Allah gave the Muhajirun from the wealth of Banu al-Nadir, so the meaning returns to them.

His saying: ﴿and prefer them over themselves﴾ means: they give precedence to the Muhajirun over themselves.

His saying: ﴿even though they themselves were in privation﴾ means: poverty and need. It is well known, by the narration of Abu Hurairah, that one of the Ansar hosted a poor man, and he had nothing beyond what he and his household and children ate. In another narration: that man had been hungry for three days and found nothing, and the Messenger of Allah sought something for him in the houses of his wives and found none, so this Ansari hosted him, took him to his home, and said to his household: "Put the children to sleep and extinguish the lamp" under the pretext of improvement. They did so, and the two of them began to extend their hands and strike upon the dish, so that the guest would think they were eating, though they were not. They did this, and the guest ate until he was full. When he went in the morning to the Prophet, he said: "Allah was amazed at your deed last night," and Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

It is well known that the Prophet said to the Ansar: "Indeed you are abundant at times of fear, and few at times of greed."

His saying: ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul﴾ means: from the miserliness of his soul. ﴿It is those who are the successful﴾ means: the felicitous, the victorious. It is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that a man said to him: "I cannot give any of my wealth, for I fear miserliness." He said: "That is miserliness, and miserliness is a dreadful thing. Rather, stinginess (shuh) is that you take wealth not by its right." It was also said: bukhl is when one withholds his own wealth, and shuh is when one withholds the wealth of others. Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: ﴿protected from the stinginess of his soul﴾ means: the greed of his soul. It was also said: the desire of his soul. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is withholding zakah. From Ibn Zayd: it is that one takes what he is not permitted to take, and withholds what it is not lawful for him to withhold.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 10:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And those who came after them﴾ are the Successors (al-tabi'un). It was also said: they are those who believe until the Day of Resurrection.

And His words: ﴿They say, "Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place in our hearts any resentment (ghill) toward those who believe"﴾ — ghill meaning treachery and malice. In the verse there is evidence that seeking mercy for the earlier generations (al-salaf), invoking good for them, and refraining from mentioning them with evil is a sign of the believers. It is narrated that a man came to Malik ibn Anas and began to disparage a group of the Companions, such as Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and others. He said to him: "Are you among the poor Emigrants (al-fuqara' al-muhajirin) who were driven out of their homes and their wealth?" He said: "No." He said: "Are you among those who settled in the abode and the faith before them?" He said: "No." Then he said: "I testify that you are not among those who came after them, saying, 'Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith.'"

It is also narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: "Whoever disparages the Companions and mentions them with evil has no share in the fay'," and he recited these three verses. It is narrated that Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz was asked about what took place among the Companions of fighting and the shedding of blood, and he said: "Those are blood which God has cleansed my hands from, so I do not like to dip my tongue in it."

It is well known that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When my Companions are mentioned, hold back; and when fate (al-qadar) is mentioned, hold back." The meaning of this is refraining from mentioning their faults, not refraining from mentioning their virtues. In some narrations: "When the stars are mentioned, hold back."

And His words: ﴿Our Lord, You are indeed Kind and Merciful﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 11:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have you not considered those who have pretended hypocrisy?﴾ They are ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, ʿAbd Allah ibn Nufayl, Zayd ibn Rifaʿa, and others.

And His saying: ﴿They say to their brothers who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture﴾ there are two opinions regarding it. One of them: they are the Banu al-Nadir, and the hypocrites said that to them before they were expelled.

The other opinion: they are the Banu Qurayza, and the hypocrites said that to them after the Banu al-Nadir had been expelled.

And His saying: ﴿If you are expelled, we will surely leave with you﴾ meaning: if you are expelled from Medina, we will surely leave with you in the fighting.

And His saying: ﴿And we will not obey anyone against you, ever﴾ meaning: we will not obey Muhammad (ﷺ) against you.

And His saying: ﴿And if you are fought, we will surely help you﴾ its meaning: and if [Muhammad] fights you, we will surely be with you in the fighting.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah testifies that indeed they are liars﴾ meaning: in this statement.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 12:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If they are expelled, they will not go out with them﴾ means: if the Jews are expelled, the hypocrites will not go out with them.

And His saying: ﴿And if they are fought, they will not help them﴾ means: if the Jews are fought, the hypocrites will not help them.

And His saying: ﴿And if they help them, they will surely turn their backs; then they will not be helped﴾. It may be asked: how did He say ﴿they will not help them﴾ and then say ﴿And if they help them﴾? If God, exalted is He, has informed that they will not help them, how is it permissible that they help them? The answer has several aspects. The first: His saying ﴿they will not help them﴾ refers to a group of the hypocrites, and His saying ﴿And if they help them﴾ means among other people of them, namely those who did not say that statement.

The second aspect: His saying ﴿they will not help them﴾ means: willingly. And His saying ﴿And if they help them﴾ means: under compulsion.

The third aspect: His saying ﴿they will not help them﴾ means: they will not persist in their help. And His saying ﴿And if they help them﴾ means: they help them at the beginning.

The fourth aspect, as stated by al-Zajjaj: it is that they will not help them in the manner God, exalted is He, has said. And His saying ﴿And if they help them﴾ means: they intend to help them; ﴿they will surely turn their backs﴾ means: they will be routed, and that is by what God, exalted is He, casts into their hearts of terror.

And His saying ﴿then they will not be helped﴾ means: the Jews will not be helped.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 13:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, you are more fearsome in their breasts than Allah﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: That is, you are more feared in their breasts than Allah, since they fear you in ways they do not fear Him.

And His words: ﴿That is because they are a people who do not understand﴾, meaning: they do not know the greatness and power of Allah, so they would fear Him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 14–15:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿They will not fight you all together except in fortified towns or from behind walls﴾. This means: they cannot face you in open combat [and confront you with it], and they fight you only within fortresses and from behind walls, out of fear for themselves and so that terror enters their hearts.

His words: ﴿Their enmity among themselves is intense﴾. Mujahid said: this means that they say among themselves, "We will do such-and-such, and we will do such-and-such."

And His words: ﴿You think they are united, but their hearts are divided﴾. This means: the hypocrites never sincerely side with the Jews, nor do the Jews sincerely side with the hypocrites.

And His words: ﴿That is because they are a people who do not reason﴾. That is, they do not reflect with their intellects, so they are in the position of one who has no intellect.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 14–15:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿They will not fight you all together except in fortified towns or from behind walls﴾. This means: they cannot face you in open combat [and confront you with it], and they fight you only within fortresses and from behind walls, out of fear for themselves and so that terror enters their hearts.

His words: ﴿Their enmity among themselves is intense﴾. Mujahid said: this means that they say among themselves, "We will do such-and-such, and we will do such-and-such."

And His words: ﴿You think they are united, but their hearts are divided﴾. This means: the hypocrites never sincerely side with the Jews, nor do the Jews sincerely side with the hypocrites.

And His words: ﴿That is because they are a people who do not reason﴾. That is, they do not reflect with their intellects, so they are in the position of one who has no intellect.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 16:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Like the Shaytan (Satan) when he says to man, "Disbelieve."﴾ That is: the likeness of these hypocrites together with the Jews is like the likeness of the Shaytan together with the disbeliever. Most of the exegetes hold that this disbeliever was a man from the Children of Israel who worshipped Allah, may He be exalted, in a hermitage (ṣawma'a) for a long time, and his name was Barṣīṣā al-ʿĀbid (Barsisa the Worshipper). Among the Children of Israel there were three brothers who had a beautiful sister who had some slight affliction (lumam), and it is said she was ill. A journey came up for them, so they said: "We will entrust our sister to so-and-so the worshipper, so that he may look after her until we return." In another narration: he would supplicate for her and attend to her; if she died, he would bury her, and if she recovered, she would remain with him until we return. So they entrusted her to him with difficulty, and he attended to her until she recovered. Then the Shaytan came to him and made it seem good to him to have intercourse with her, so he did, and she became pregnant by him. Then the Shaytan came and said: "You will be exposed when her brothers return, so kill her, bury her, and say that she died." So he did that and buried her at the base of his hermitage. When the brothers returned and came to him, he told them that she had died, and they believed him. Then the Shaytan showed them in a dream that the worshipper had killed their sister and buried her in such-and-such a place. They came to that place, dug, and extracted their sister, slain. They went and reported that to the king, so the king came with the people and they brought the worshipper down from his hermitage to kill him. The Shaytan came to him and said: "I am the one who did to you what was done. Obey me and I will save you." He said: "What should I do?" He said: "Prostrate to me one prostration." So he did, and he was killed upon disbelief. This verse was revealed concerning this story. ʿAṭiyya has narrated something close to this from Ibn ʿAbbas. Some have related this story with a chain going back to the Messenger (ﷺ), by the narration of Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, with wordings close to this in meaning. The Shaykh said: Abu ʿAli al-Shafiʿi informed us of this in Makkah, Ibn Firas informed us, Abu Jaʿfar al-Dībilī informed us, Saʿid ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Makhzumi informed us, from Sufyan.

His statement: ﴿So when he disbelieved, he said, "Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ This is like His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And when the two hosts sighted each other, he turned back on his heels and said, "Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I see what you do not see. Indeed, I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment."﴾ It is said that his fear was of punishment in this world, not of punishment in the Hereafter. It is also said that it was the fear of punishment in the Hereafter, except that his fear does not benefit him due to lack of faith. It is also said that the verse was revealed concerning all disbelievers, not a specific disbeliever, and the well-known view is the first opinion.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So the final outcome of both of them is that they will be in the Fire, abiding therein﴾. That is: the final outcome of the disbeliever and Iblis. (Abiding therein) means: remaining therein forever.

And His saying: ﴿And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers﴾. That is: the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 18:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah. And let every soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow.﴾ Qatadah said: "He continued to bring the Hour near until He made it as tomorrow."

And His saying: ﴿And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ The command to piety (taqwa) here is in the manner of emphasis.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 19:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves﴾. That is: they abandoned the command of Allah, so He abandoned them from His regard and His mercy. It was said that its meaning is: they abandoned seeking their share for themselves in the Hereafter through what they abandoned of the command of Allah, and it is attributed to Allah, exalted is He, because their abandonment of seeking their share for themselves, and their losing it, was on account of what was directed at them from the command of Allah. It was also said that its meaning is: He made them heedless of their own share as a punishment for them. Al-Nahhas said: "It is correct in Arabic to say: nasiyahum fulan (meaning: so-and-so abandoned them), in the sense of tarakahum (he left them). But it is not correct to say: ansahum (in the sense of tarakahum)."

And His saying: ﴿Those are the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqun)﴾. That is: those who go out of obedience to Allah.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal. The companions of Paradise are the ones who are triumphant.﴾ That is, the ones who are saved.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 21:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and split asunder from fear of Allah﴾. That is: if We were to give it discernment and understanding.

It has been said: this is mentioned by way of illustration (tamthil), not as a literal reality. But according to the People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah), Allah, exalted is He, has knowledge in the dead and inanimate things that people do not comprehend. He has said in another place: ﴿But you do not understand their glorification﴾, and this is evidence for what we have mentioned before.

And His statement: ﴿khashi'an﴾ means humbled, submissive. It has been said: ﴿mutasaddi'an﴾ means split, cracked from fear of Allah.

And His statement: ﴿And these examples We present to the people that they may give thought﴾ means: that they may reflect and ponder.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾ means the secret and the open. It has also been said that "the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed" means what has been and what will be.

And His saying: ﴿He is the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾. We have already explained it.

He said: ﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no god, the King﴾, meaning: the one capable over all things.

And His saying: ﴿al-Quddus (the Holy One)﴾, i.e. the Pure. It was also said: the one free of every deficiency and defect. It was also said: al-Quddus means the one who is sanctified, meaning the angels sanctify Him and glorify Him. In the angels' glorification it is said: "Most Holy, Most Pure, Lord of the angels and the Spirit." From this comes Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), and from this comes Hazirat al-Quds, which is Paradise. Ru'bah said:

"I called upon the Lord of Might, the Holy,
a call of one who does not strike the naqus (bell)."

And His saying: ﴿al-Salam (the Giver of Peace)﴾. Qatadah said: its meaning is that He is free from calamities and defects. Mujahid said: He has kept people safe from His injustice. In some reports it is related that the Prophet said: "As-Salam is one of the names of Allah, [and He placed it] among you, so spread it."

And His saying: ﴿al-Mu'min (the Granter of Security)﴾. Concerning it there are several opinions. The first: He grants security to the believers from the Fire and the punishment. The second: the believers are safe from His injustice, so He is al-Mu'min. The third: He bore witness to His own oneness, so He is al-Mu'min in this sense, and His witnessing to His own oneness is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He﴾.

And His saying: ﴿al-Muhaymin (the Guardian)﴾. Qatadah said: it means al-Shahid (the Witness). Some of them said: it is al-Amin (the Trustworthy), and the meaning of His being trustworthy is that He does not lose the deeds of the servants, as if the deeds of the servants are in His trust and He does not lose them. It was also said: it is al-Raqib (the Watchful). It was also said: the origin of al-Muhaymin is al-mu'aymin, except that the hamzah was changed into a haa', like their saying "araqtu al-ma'a" and "haraqtuhu" (I poured out the water).

And His saying: ﴿al-'Aziz (the Mighty)﴾, i.e. the Overpowering. It was also said: the Subduer. It was also said: the Invincible.

The poet said concerning al-Muhaymin:

"A King over the throne of heaven, the Guardian,
before whose might faces are humbled and prostrate."

And His saying: ﴿al-Jabbar (the Compeller)﴾, i.e. He compels creation to His will and purpose. It was also said: al-Jabbar means al-'Azim (the Great). It was also said: He is the One who is beyond the reach of imagination and perception.

It is said: a date palm that is jabbarah is one that is tall, so that it cannot be reached by hands.

His saying: ﴿al-Mutakabbir (the Supreme in Majesty)﴾, i.e. al-Kabir (the Great). It was also said: al-Mutakabbir is the one who exalts Himself and magnifies Himself. This is praiseworthy in the attributes of Allah but blameworthy in the attributes of created beings, because created beings are never free of deficiency, so it is not fitting for them to magnify themselves and exalt themselves. Allah, may He be exalted, is not subject to any deficiency, so His praising Himself and magnifying Himself is valid.

It was also said: He praised Himself so that His creatures would know their praise of Him, in order to reward them for it, since it is not possible for harm or benefit to reach Him.

And His saying: ﴿Glory be to Allah above what they associate with Him﴾. We have explained this in many places.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 24:

His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿He is Allah, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner﴾. That is: the one who determines things and brings them into existence.

As for His words ﴿al-Bari'﴾ (the Originator): it is said that it has the meaning of "al-Khaliq" (the Creator), by way of emphasis. It is also said that its meaning is the one who gives life after death. The poet said:

(And every soul, in its soundness... Allah causes it to die, then brings it back into being.)

This was mentioned by Abu al-Hasan ibn Faris.

As for His words ﴿al-Musawwir﴾ (the Fashioner): it is the known shaping (taswir), He shapes every creature as He wills. It is also said that taswir is a specific composition in a specific place within creation.

As for His words, the Exalted: ﴿To Him belong the most beautiful names﴾. Al-husna is the feminine form of al-ahsan (the most beautiful), and here it carries the meaning of al-'ulya (the highest).

As for His words: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, and He is the Almighty, the Wise﴾, its meaning is apparent. It has been narrated in some of the musnads, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the Greatest Name of Allah is in the last three verses of Surat al-Hashr." And Allah knows best.
